---
title: "Appendix 3C: OR and MEM Comparison"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Stata

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
// Health and Retirement Study 2006 //
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/hrs06", clear

logit diabetes c.age i.black c.bmi i.woman i.ed4cat, or cformat(%6.4f)
est store diabmod
<</dd_do>>
```

## R

```{r}
library(haven)           # import Stata data and labels
library(dplyr)           # data manipulation
library(marginaleffects) # predictions and marginal effects
library(questionr)       # odds ratios

# Health and Retirement Study 2006
hrs <- read_dta("https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/hrs06.dta")

# Treat binary/nominal variables as factors using their value labels
hrs <- hrs |>
  mutate(black = as_factor(black), woman = as_factor(woman), ed4cat = as_factor(ed4cat))

diabmod <- glm(diabetes ~ age + black + bmi + woman + ed4cat,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), data = hrs)
odds.ratio(diabmod, level = .95, digits = 4)
```

:::

Keep the OR for Black (1.6465) and the OR for BMI (1.1060) in mind for the following sections

## Compute MEM and OR for effect of race

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Stata

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
* Compute OR for effect of race
est restore diabmod
mtable, at(black=(0 1)) decimal(7) atmeans post
mlincom 2 - 1 // MEM

di 0.2479810 / (1 - 0.2479810) // Odds when black = 1
di 0.1668597 / (1 - 0.1668597) // Odds when black = 0
di %6.4f .32975364 / .20027803 // Odds ratio
<</dd_do>>
```

## R

```{r}
# Compute OR for effect of race: predictions with other variables at means/modes
prs_black <- predictions(diabmod, newdata = datagrid(black = c("White", "Black")))
prs_black

comparisons(diabmod, variables = "black", newdata = "mean") # MEM

odds_black <- prs_black$estimate / (1 - prs_black$estimate)
odds_black                   # Odds when black = 0 and black = 1
odds_black[2] / odds_black[1] # Odds ratio
```

:::

::: {.callout-note icon="false" appearance="simple"}
Reminder---odds (Ω) are just a transformation of a probability (π):

$$\Omega = \frac{\pi}{1 - \pi}$$
:::

## Compute MEM and OR for effect of BMI

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Stata

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
* Compute OR for effect of BMI
est restore diabmod
sum bmi

mtable, at(bmi=(27.83901 28.83901)) decimal(7) atmeans post
mlincom 2 - 1 // MEM

di 0.1924603 / (1 - 0.1924603) // Odds when bmi = mean + 1
di 0.1772895 / (1 - 0.1772895) // Odds when bmi = mean
di %6.4f .23832921 / .21549439 // Odds ratio
<</dd_do>>
```

## R

```{r}
# Compute OR for effect of BMI: predictions with other variables at means/modes
summary(hrs$bmi)
mean_bmi <- mean(hrs$bmi, na.rm = TRUE)

prs_bmi <- predictions(diabmod, newdata = datagrid(bmi = c(mean_bmi, mean_bmi + 1)))
prs_bmi

comparisons(diabmod, variables = list(bmi = 1), newdata = "mean") # MEM

odds_bmi <- prs_bmi$estimate / (1 - prs_bmi$estimate)
odds_bmi                 # Odds when bmi = mean and bmi = mean + 1
odds_bmi[2] / odds_bmi[1] # Odds ratio
```

:::

Given that the OR is simply a different way to present the same information a MEM summarizes---which would you prefer to interpret? Which is easier to understand?
